mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over the next month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns within the following 20-day window.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat when FEDFUNDS increases as specified, or the effect is not statistically significant in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market strengthening that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% while UNRATE falls by at least 0.1 percentage points within the next month
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return in the 60-day window when the trigger occurs, or the interaction effect rank is below 0.05 in walk-forward evaluation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 2% suggests accelerating demand growth that anticipates higher corporate profits and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: More than 40% of triggered 5-day windows show non-positive returns, or the effect is not robust to alternative inflation regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer confidence proxies (not available in evidence - so omit) would typically imply supply-side weakness, but in this restricted evidence set we posit that a large drop in RSAFS (retail sales) below -3% in a month predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by more than 3% in a single month
failure_condition: Frequent positive 20-day returns when RSAFS declines as specified, or the effect is spurious in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) remains below 2% for three consecutive months, the market anticipates lower policy tightening, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL stays below 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative or flat when the trigger is met, or the pattern reverses in subsequent months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-standard-deviation increase in payrolls (PAYEMS) followed by a sustained decline in unemployment (UNRATE) creates expectations of wage growth and reduced labor market frictions, producing positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than one standard deviation above its monthly mean while UNRATE decreases by 0.2 percentage pts
failure_condition: No significant positive return in the 60-day horizon under the specified interaction, or the interaction rank is weak in walk-forward tests.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a steady-state monetary policy (FEDFUNDS stabilizes above 5% for two months) reduces discounting uncertainty and supports positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS remains above 5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Frequent negative returns when the trigger occurs, or the effect is not robust across multiple policy regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of 3% or more indicates weakening manufacturing momentum that typically precedes S&P 500 declines in the next 20-day forward period.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by 3% or more in a month
failure_condition: More than 70% of triggered windows show non-negative returns, or the effect is not statistically significant in walk-forward testing.
